what_happened: Scene: layout 10, wide printed tea mug_8 on a dark wooden open shelf (lime distractor), machine CoffeeMachine051 off to the right. Stage 0: the gripper approached the mug with open fingers and closed at 88-96 while the mug wall was still a few cm beyond the fingertips (wrist 88-112: mug in front of, not between, the fingers); no contact. The fingers then stayed closed (width 0.001) for the rest of the episode - they never reopened. From 128 to 1200 the arm drifted back and forth 10-30 cm in front of the mug (it grows and shrinks in the wrist view at 150-1196), sometimes swinging right towards the machine side (250-450) and coming back, but never got near enough to touch it with the closed fingers. The mug never moved; stage 1 was never reached.
causal_chain: premature close a few cm short of the mug (88) -> gripper never reopens -> ~1100 steps of approach/retreat in front of the mug with closed fingers -> mug never picked -> timeout
self_recovery: none effective: repeated approaches, but with the fingers still closed, so no new grasp was possible.

packet_facts: close_events: 88 on_nothing; gripper width 0.001-0.003 from 112 to 1200 (never reopened)

uncertain_about: Why the close was triggered early (depth misjudgement on this large mug is a guess).
